title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). Grothendieck is axiomatising a combinatorial 'analysis situs', in the spirit of the tame topology programme of the Esquisse. The ingredients are as follows.
- A 'multigraphe' M: a set of pieces or cells with an order ≤ (closure/incidence), a strict relation ⟨<<°⟩ (something like 'strongly below' or 'interior incidence') and a relation |∘| (roughly 'apart/disjoint').
- An 'adhésion'/'atelier' (𝓕, M, ◁, <<°, |∘|): 𝓕 is a set of 'fragments' (closed unions of pieces), ◁ is an incidence between 𝓕 and M, and F̃ ⊂ M is the set of pieces of F.
- 𝓕 is ordered by ≤ and has arbitrary Sup and nonempty Inf. It is modelled on the lattice of subcomplexes of a cell complex, i.e. essentially down-closed subsets of the face poset.

Previous page. A sub-multigraph M' ⊂ M is a subset that is
- ≤-down-closed, and
- such that X <<° Y' ≤ Y with X, Y ∈ M' forces Y' ∈ M'.
The restricted atelier is 𝓕' = {F : F̃ ⊂ M'}, and 𝓕' → 𝓕 preserves arbitrary Sups and nonempty Infs.

This page, part 1: heredity remarks.
- If |∘| on M is definable in terms of <<°, the same need not hold for the induced relations on M'. The definition presumably quantifies over pieces that may fall outside M'.
- It does hold if M' is <<°-closed, but often M' will not be.
- On the other hand, a 'Lieu' L of M contained in M' remains a Lieu of M' (reading uncertain).
- Hence the properties 'dirigé' (via the characterisation on his p. 23), 'quasi-ensembliste' and 'ensembliste' pass from M to sub-multigraphs.

This page, part 2: homomorphisms. He announces that he is forced to study homomorphisms of ateliers. These are maps respecting not only <<° and |∘| but also the membership/incidence ∈. He sets up two ateliers (𝓕, M, …) and (𝓕', M', …) and is about to define the maps f: 𝓕 → 𝓕' that will count as homomorphisms.

Next page. The conditions are:
- f is monotone and preserves all Sups, so f is determined by a monotone f_M: M → 𝓕'. Any monotone f_M extends when fragments are of finite type.
- f preserves Infs, reducing to f_M(X) ∩ f_M(Y) = Sup_{Z ∈ X∩Y} f_M(Z), the analogue of the fragmentation formula X_i ∩ X_j = ⋃_{k∈ij} X_k.

In modern terms, these are complete-lattice morphisms between Alexandrov-type (completely distributive) lattices of subcomplexes. They play the role of cellular/'tame' maps described combinatorially on face posets, close to frame/coframe homomorphisms in locale theory.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. The page consists of hedged remarks ('il n'est pas clair', '...') and an unfinished heredity check, with no proofs given.

ideas.what: Heredity of structural properties (definability of |∘| via <<°, 'dirigé', 'quasi-ensembliste', 'ensembliste') under passage to sub-multigraphs (down-closed, <<°-convex subsets)
ideas.modern_name: Restriction to subcomplexes / down-closed subposets of face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in combinatorial topology (face posets of regular CW complexes)

ideas.what: Homomorphisms of 'ateliers' as maps of fragment lattices preserving arbitrary Sups and Infs, determined by their values on pieces
ideas.modern_name: Complete lattice / frame-coframe homomorphisms; cellular maps described on face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Locale theory (Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell, Johnstone 1970s–80s); Alexandrov topologies
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a transitional note. It contains routine heredity remarks for sub-structures and the start of a definition of homomorphisms between his combinatorial 'ateliers'. It documents the internal development of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic analysis situs, but contains no result beyond standard lattice/poset facts.
transcription_corrections: 'qu'il en soit de =' → '=' is Grothendieck's shorthand for 'même': 'qu'il en soit de même dans M''.
'mais en sera-t-il [?] ainsi [?] si M'' → 'mais ce sera le cas si M''.
'(mais bien sûrement, M' ne le sera pas...)' → probably '(mais bien souvent, M' ne le sera pas...)'.
'stand. dirige' / 'caractéristique M_0 dirige, page 23' → likely 'M est dirigé ... (caractérisation des M dirigés, page 23)'.
'[?] si M est quasi-ensembliste' → 'de même si M est quasi-ensembliste' (the ampersand-like sign).
'Je suis amené maintenant à [?] des études (contraintes)' → probably 'Je suis amené maintenant à étudier (contraint et forcé) la notion d'homomorphismes entre ateliers'.
'Ci-dessous les appellations provisoires' → likely 'D'où les appellations provisoires "homomorphismes"'.
F should be calligraphic 𝓕 (fragments), consistent with the neighbouring pages.
The 'anneau M' ⊃ L' line is doubtful; it more likely concerns a Lieu L contained in M' remaining a Lieu of M'.
